tagline: Conversion collapsed 74% right after Black Friday deploy. Save the checkout flow.

incidents.title: Invisible Primary Action
incidents.hook: Users are adding items to cart, but only 4% ever tap the checkout button.
incidents.alert: CONVERSION CRASH — Mobile cart checkout rate down 72% post redesign
incidents.stakes_line: $120,000 in abandoned carts accumulates every fifteen minutes.

evidence.label: HOTJAR HEATMAP
evidence.content: Users repeatedly tapping the promotional coupon banner instead of checkout CTA.

evidence.label: VIEWPORT WIREFRAME
evidence.content: Checkout button styled as gray ghost outline pushed below the fold on iOS Safari.

evidence.label: CUSTOMER SUPPORT
evidence.content: Support rep: Chat queue is filled with elderly shoppers asking how to pay.

incidents.question: What is the single highest-impact design intervention?

options.text: Pin a high-contrast solid sticky CTA with clear label 'Proceed to Checkout' at screen bottom.
options.outcome: Checkout completion immediately surges back above 68% across all devices.
options.why: Sticky high-contrast buttons guarantee clear affordance regardless of device scroll height.

options.text: Add an animated popup modal prompting users to enter their email before paying.
options.outcome: Cart abandonment increases by an additional 15% due to modal fatigue.
options.why: Interruptive modals add friction at the highest-anxiety step in the funnel.

options.text: Redesign the entire cart color scheme and font hierarchy from scratch.
options.outcome: Hours of design debate while the Black Friday shopping window closes.
options.why: Complete redesign during an active conversion crisis introduces unknown risks.

options.text: Make the coupon promo banner flash brightly to guide user attention down.
options.outcome: Users tap the coupon even more, confusing checkout with discount entry.
options.why: Flashing elements worsen cognitive overload and distract from the primary conversion goal.

debrief.concept: Unambiguous visual hierarchy for primary actions
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Make the primary action impossible to miss: one button, solid color, above the fold.
debrief.why_best_works: Clear contrast and persistent positioning eliminate scanning friction for buyers.
debrief.real_world_note: Amazon one-click checkout succeeded by removing all competing visual elements.
debrief.next_teaser: Users can pay, but return rates are spiking because variant selection is ambiguous.

incidents.title: Ambiguous Variant Selector
incidents.hook: Customers ordering shoes are receiving wrong sizes and returning 52% of orders.
incidents.alert: RETURN RATE SPIKE — 52% of shoes returned due to wrong size ordered
incidents.stakes_line: Warehouse restocking fees and shipping losses will bankrupt promotional margins.

evidence.label: SIZE PICKER COMPONENT
evidence.content: Selected size chip uses light gray border; unselected chips use slightly lighter gray.

evidence.label: SESSION REPLAY LOG
evidence.content: Users tapping size 9, then tapping size 10 to check if state changed, then buying 9.

evidence.label: WAREHOUSE OPS
evidence.content: Ops Manager: Over 400 return boxes arrived this morning marked 'Size not what I clicked'.

incidents.question: How do you eliminate the selection ambiguity immediately?

options.text: Use heavy contrast fill with checkmark for selected state and plain text for unselected.
options.outcome: Session confusion drops to zero; return rate normalizes to baseline under 4%.
options.why: Dual visual indicators (bold fill plus checkmark icon) eliminate state ambiguity.

options.text: Add a tooltip explaining that light gray means selected and white means available.
options.outcome: Users do not read tooltips on mobile touchscreens; wrong orders continue.
options.why: Good UI communicates state intuitively without requiring instructional manual reading.

options.text: Replace the chips with a 20-item native dropdown select menu.
options.outcome: Functional, but tap friction increases by 2 taps and conversion drops 8%.
options.why: Dropdowns hide available options and increase interaction cost compared to chips.

options.text: Prompt user with a confirmation modal: 'Are you absolutely sure you want size 9?'
options.outcome: Adds checkout anxiety and causes buyers to second-guess their purchase.
options.why: Confirmation dialogs should be reserved for irreversible actions, not routine selections.

debrief.rule_of_thumb: Never rely on subtle color tint alone to show selection; add shape or icon contrast.
debrief.why_best_works: Multiple perceptual signals ensure clarity across different screen brightness levels.
debrief.real_world_note: Material Design and Apple HIG mandate distinct elevation and shape for active states.
debrief.next_teaser: Shoppers can select sizes, but blind users are filing ADA accessibility complaints.

incidents.title: Screen Reader Traps & ADA Crisis
incidents.hook: Assistive tech users cannot close the filter drawer and legal received an ADA warning.
incidents.alert: ADA COMPLIANCE ALERT — Legal notice of non-compliance received from advocacy group
incidents.stakes_line: Statutory damages and brand reputation threatened if not remediated immediately.

evidence.label: ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT
evidence.content: Filter drawer lacks role='dialog', aria-modal='true', and focus-trap management.

evidence.label: DOM INSPECTOR
evidence.content:
Close button is rendered as `
X
` with no aria-label or tabindex.

evidence.label: LEGAL COUNSEL
evidence.content: General Counsel: Fix the focus trap and keyboard accessibility today to cure violation.

incidents.question: What is the correct accessibility engineering fix?

options.text: Refactor to semantic `<button>`, add aria-label='Close filters', and trap focus within modal.
options.outcome: Lighthouse accessibility score jumps to 100; screen reader navigation passes audit.
options.why: Semantic elements provide built-in keyboard accessibility and screen reader hooks.

options.text: Install a third-party accessibility overlay widget snippet into the HTML head tag.
options.outcome: Blind users complain widget breaks their readers; accessibility lawsuits increase.
options.why: Accessibility overlays do not fix broken underlying DOM semantics and anger users.

options.text: Remove the filter drawer entirely and only show unfiltered product listings.
options.outcome: Users cannot narrow 10,000 products; average search time climbs to 14 minutes.
options.why: Destroying core functionality rather than making it accessible degrades everyone's UX.

options.text: Add a disclaimer text in footer saying 'Best experienced with Google Chrome'.
options.outcome: Does nothing to address legal liability or assist disabled customers.
options.why: Disclaimers do not satisfy ADA compliance or WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards.

debrief.rule_of_thumb: Use real HTML buttons and manage keyboard focus; never fake UI with clickable divs.
debrief.why_best_works: Native browser elements carry decades of assistive accessibility technology support.
debrief.real_world_note: Major retailers faced multi-million dollar class actions over inaccessible drawer menus.
debrief.next_teaser: Legal is satisfied, but marketing added deceptive countdown timers causing churn.

incidents.title: Dark Pattern Backlash
incidents.hook: Fake urgency countdown and pre-checked monthly subscriptions trigger viral tweetstorm.
incidents.alert: PR DISASTER — Viral tweet #ScammyCheckout reaches 4.2M views
incidents.stakes_line: Brand trust is collapsing, and credit card processors threaten chargeback fines.

evidence.label: CHECKOUT CHECKBOX
evidence.content: Pre-checked box: 'Enroll me in $29.99/mo VIP Club' hidden in tiny 10px gray font.

evidence.label: CHARGEBACK METRIC
evidence.content: Stripe chargeback dispute rate hits 1.8% (Visa cutoff threshold is 1.0%).

evidence.label: HEAD OF MARKETING
evidence.content: Marketing: The pre-check raised revenue for 2 weeks, but now our ratings dropped to 1.4 stars.

incidents.question: What is the ethical, long-term brand restoration decision?

options.text: Remove pre-checked opt-in, make subscription explicit choice, and refund disputed charges.
options.outcome: Public sentiment shifts positively; chargeback rates plummet below penalty thresholds.
options.why: Honest opt-in builds enduring customer lifetime value and stops processor bans.

options.text: Make the unsubscribe link harder to find to prevent existing members from leaving.
options.outcome: FTC launches consumer protection inquiry; payment gateway freezes funds.
options.why: Roach motel dark patterns attract aggressive regulatory enforcement and fines.

options.text: Change the countdown timer to restart every 3 minutes so it looks real.
options.outcome: Tech-savvy users record the loop, posting more evidence of fake urgency.
options.why: Fake countdown timers destroy credibility the moment a shopper refreshes the page.

options.text: Offer a 10% coupon to anyone who deletes their critical tweet.
options.outcome: Screenshots of the bribe get retweeted, compounding brand embarrassment.
options.why: Bribing critics without fixing deceptive product design backfires publicly.

debrief.concept: Transparent value exchange vs. manipulative dark patterns
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Subscriptions must always be explicit opt-in; tricks create chargebacks, not loyalty.
debrief.why_best_works: Customers gladly pay for value they consciously selected; deception produces churn.
debrief.real_world_note: FTC 'Click to Cancel' regulations penalize deceptive recurring billing workflows.
debrief.next_teaser: Final challenge: five independent teams built conflicting navigation and broken states.

incidents.title: Design System Fragmented Chaos
incidents.hook: 12 different button styles, conflicting primary colors, and broken responsive breakpoints.
incidents.alert: PRODUCTION DRIFT — 42 conflicting CSS button classes detected in production build
incidents.stakes_line: Release velocity has slowed to a crawl as teams rewrite custom CSS for every view.

evidence.label: CSS BUNDLE AUDIT
evidence.content: Found 18 variations of blue hex codes and 7 contradictory modal frameworks in bundle.

evidence.label: COMPONENT MATRIX
evidence.content: Settings page looks like Android 2014, Checkout looks like iOS, Home looks custom.

evidence.label: VP OF PRODUCT
evidence.content: VP Product: Ship velocity is down 60%. We need a single unified source of truth now.

incidents.question: What is the strategic foundation to unify the design system forever?

options.text: Establish centralized design tokens for colors/spacing, deprecate rogue classes, enforce lint gates.
options.outcome: CSS bundle size shrinks 48%; development speed doubles with consistent components.
options.why: Centralized design tokens decouple styles from implementations and create single source of truth.

options.text: Allow each team to maintain their own custom style guide in Figma without syncing.
options.outcome: Fragmentation accelerates until the product looks like five separate websites.
options.why: Decentralized un-synced design libraries guarantee divergent user experiences.

options.text: Ban all CSS classes and force developers to write inline HTML styles.
options.outcome: Bundle sizes skyrocket; maintaining global theme adjustments becomes impossible.
options.why: Inline styles destroy caching, reusability, and maintainability at scale.

options.text: Schedule a monthly committee meeting to manually approve every UI change.
options.outcome: Design bottleneck paralyzes releases while rogue styling continues in branches.
options.why: Bureaucratic gatekeeping fails without automated design token tooling.

debrief.concept: Design tokens as the single source of truth
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Tokenize your design primitives; automate consistency at compile time, not in committee.
debrief.why_best_works: Tokens bridge design tools and codebases with zero translation friction.
debrief.real_world_note: Figma Tokens and Tailwind config enable thousands of engineers to share one design language.
debrief.next_teaser: Case closed! The design system is harmonized and conversion has recovered.
